Fig. 2. Qualitative comparison on representative samples. Images are cropped and zoomed for better visualization. Prominent regions are highlighted with boxes.

Fig. 1. Schematic illustration of DINO-Med3D framework. Stage I aligns the pretrained 2D DINOv3 backbone with volumetric medical data via the Inter-slice Context Embedding (ICE) module and a pseudo-3D proxy task. Stage II freezes the aligned backbone and introduces a dual-stream architecture: a Volumetric Context Encoding Stream leveraging LoRA and lightweight 3D adapters for semantic reasoning, and a parallel Detail-Recovery Stream for capturing high-frequency boundary information. Finally, features are integrated via Adaptive Gated Fusion (AGF) for dense prediction.
